correctness.rationale: The ordinary matching complex is formed from every set of pairwise disjoint edges in GP(12,5), not only perfect-matchable subsets. Independently generated the entire matching-count polynomial (1,36,558,4884,26613,93888,216228,320256,293436,155024,41832,4608,120), total 1,157,484 augmented faces. Source C++ explicitly builds all matchings, pairs along indexed edges, topologically sorts all 8,344,008 augmented Hasse arrows, and eliminates signed 7-to-8 incidence pairs. Its critical cells are one 0, 132 in dimension 7, 40 in 8. Independently loaded its actual 132×40 Morse boundary matrix via GitHub blob and performed exact unimodular unit-pivot row/column operations: 34 pivots of ±1, remaining block all zero, proving its Smith factors (1×34,0×6), no torsion. The 7-skeleton is ∨132 S7, so the integral degrees classify all 8-cell attaching maps; 34 cell pairs cancel to yield 98 S7 and 6 S8.

value.rationale: The ordinary edge-matching complex of the symmetric Nauru GP(12,5) graph is a canonical graph complex. Determining both integral 98 and 6 sphere multiplicities in two adjacent high dimensions, and excluding torsion, supplies a natural missing exact invariant that the earlier perfect-matching and vertex-independence calculations do not determine. It is a useful benchmark for future generalized-Petersen or graph-matching classification and for testing Morse methods, without requiring a universal theorem.
residual_risks: Object-specific and certificate-intensive; no symmetry representation or all-GP formula is claimed.

final_claim: The ordinary matching complex M(GP(12,5)) of the 24-vertex Nauru graph has integral homotopy type 98 copies S7 wedge 6 copies S8.
